key_insight: Wind shear and veer lower actuator-disk power mainly by combining simple rotor-wind-speed changes with aerodynamic induction effects, and these losses grow roughly linearly with their magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Power prediction models for wind turbines should account for both geometric inflow changes and induction-driven aerodynamics in realistic atmospheric boundary layer conditions.
method: Concurrent-precursor LES of an actuator disk turbine in stratified ABL flows
Controlled inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently
Decomposed losses into geometric and inductive contributions
evidence_signal: The simulations show shear and veer can reduce power coefficient by more than 20%, with inductive effects making a substantial fraction of the loss.
watch_item: The findings are for actuator disk LES and simplified inflow controls, so translating them to full rotor engineering models requires care, especially near-wall and strongly nonuniform atmospheric conditions.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
